To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the renal function of the patient can be measured using either renography or DMSA scinitigraphy and that the results are sufficiently reliable that the clinician can be confident in their interpretation.

1) the relative function of a diseased kidney can be estimated from either a renogram or a DMSA scan, 2) attenuation correction is not required in most patients, 3) a difference of more than 5% is required between sequential studies to be sure that a change in renal function has occurred.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the measurement of relative renal function using 99Tcm labelled DMSA scintrigraphy and the application of this method in clinical practice.
the development of a novel approach for the measurement of renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease.
the development of a new class of non-invasive imaging techniques that are capable of providing information about the functional state of the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative renal functions can be measured by renography and by scintigraphy with DMSA and are comparable and reproducible.
the measurement of relative renal function is a useful clinical tool which can be performed with a high degree of reproducibility by renography or DMSA scinigraphy.
DMSA scinigraphy is the best available technique for measuring relative renal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measurement of relative renal function is best performed with a DMSA scan.
renography and DSA scintigraphy yield complimentary information and both can be used for the measurement of renal function, but that the results are sufficiently reliable to be clinically useful.
the relative uptake of DMSA in the kidneys is an excellent method for measuring relative renal function and can be used in place of 131I-hippurate clearance in patients with normal renal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative renal function can be measured equally accurately by either renogram or DMSA scan and the results are reproducible.
relative renal function (RRF) can be calculated by either method and is reproducible.
relative renal function can be measured with a good correlation between 99mTc-DMSA and 131I-ortho-iodohippurate (OIH) clearance.
